questions.q: What is the correct order of the three-level hierarchy described in this lesson?
options: Navigator, Work Area, Task
Task, Work Area, Navigator
Work Area, Navigator, Task
Navigator, Task, Work Area
questions.explain: The Navigator is the top-level directory, which opens a Work Area (a landing page for one function), inside which specific Tasks live.

questions.q: What is a 'work area' in Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: Just a label on a menu item with no further content
A dedicated landing page for one specific function, such as General Accounting
A type of security role
A folder on the user's desktop
questions.explain: A work area is a full landing page scoped to one function, often including a Tasks panel, infolets, and a worklist — more than just a menu label.

questions.q: What does the Tasks panel inside a work area typically do?
options: Displays the quarterly update release notes
Shows only the user's personal to-do list unrelated to the system
Lists the specific activities available in that work area, often grouped by category
Replaces the need for the Navigator entirely
questions.explain: The Tasks panel lists the activities available inside that specific work area, grouped by category, such as Journals or Period Close within General Accounting.

options: A security setting that locks an account after failed logins
A type of infolet that only shows errors
An automatic process that runs during quarterly updates
A shortcut to a common, frequent task, available directly from the home page without navigating through a work area first
questions.explain: Quick Actions surface frequent tasks (like Create Journal) directly on the home page, skipping the Navigator and Tasks panel for speed.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say understanding the Navigator/Work Area/Task hierarchy matters for later security work?
options: Because access in Oracle Fusion Security is often granted at exactly this level of granularity — a work area, specific tasks, or both
Because security has nothing to do with this hierarchy
Because only Navigator-level access can ever be restricted
Because tasks cannot be secured independently of work areas
questions.explain: Security roles often grant or restrict access at the work-area or task level, so understanding this hierarchy now helps when troubleshooting access issues later.
